Isaiah 52:7 expressly condenses the good tidings as “Thy God reigneth”; Mark 1:14–15 identifies Jesus’ pre-cross gospel with the approaching kingdom; and the gospel language applied to Abraham, wilderness Israel, and Revelation 14 shows that the term cannot be restricted to a report of already-completed death and resurrection events. The strongest counter-reading rightly makes Christ’s death and resurrection indispensable and explains 1 Corinthians 15 more directly, but it does not replace the kingdom-proclamation core; it broadens it by identifying the Christ-event as the climactic means by which God’s reign and salvation are accomplished.
